itineraries.title: Hopscotch Saturday, Free-First
itineraries.theme: Downtown Raleigh music crawl built on the free day parties
itineraries.drive_time: 0 min from downtown Raleigh; park once and walk everything
itineraries.cost_range: $0-$40 without a festival wristband; add the wristband for the night shows
itineraries.overview: Hopscotch's closing Saturday. The clever move is that most of the daytime programming is free and wristband-free — three club day parties inside a six-block radius — so you can spend the whole day on downtown music for nothing, eat well, and only decide about a wristband at dinnertime. Storms are in the forecast, which is fine: every stop here is indoors.

morning.title: NCMA-WS Presents: Southern Idiom, Expanded — free Hopscotch day party
morning.location: The Pour House Music Hall, 224 S Blount St
morning.notes: Southern roots bill with The Treasury, COGS and Mellow Swells. No wristband needed — walk in.

afternoon.title: Kings Family Show — free Hopscotch day party
afternoon.notes: Three blocks from the Pour House. Duck in and out as the lineups rotate.

afternoon.title: Jack The Radio Presents: Hopscotch Day Party
afternoon.notes: Runs in parallel with Kings — Slim's is next door to it, so bounce between the two.

afternoon.title: The ComedyWorx Matinee
afternoon.notes: An all-ages improv break if you want an hour off your feet. Skip if you'd rather keep drifting between clubs.

evening.title: Hopscotch Music Festival 2026 — Day 3 (main programming)
evening.location: City Plaza and clubs across downtown Raleigh
evening.notes: Wristband City is at Church on Morgan, 136 E. Morgan St. Cory Wong, King Princess, Soccer Mommy, Momma and Duckwrth are on this year's bill.

evening.title: Hopscotch Night #3: Horsegirl, Hiding Places, Spoils, bedrumor
evening.notes: Chicago's Horsegirl close out the Pour House.

evening.title: SNL's "Killed It At KillJoy"
evening.notes: The no-wristband alternative — free stand-up with RSVP, mature crowd. Ten minutes' walk from City Plaza.

food.place: Videri Chocolate Factory / Warehouse District cafés
food.notes: Coffee before the first day party. Check current hours — this is a walk-up recommendation, not a verified menu.

food.vegan_dish: Tofu Banh Mi ($16) or the Black Bean + Butternut Quesadilla ($15) — both vegan
food.notes: 2431-103 Crabtree Blvd. Entirely vegetarian/vegan kitchen, so nobody in the group has to negotiate. A short drive from downtown — or swap for a downtown counter if you want to stay on foot.

food.vegan_dish: Hearts of Palm & Lions Mane "Crabcakes" ($22) or the Eastern NC Style BBQ Sandwich ($17)
food.notes: Book ahead on a festival Saturday.

alternatives.good_weather: Walk — the Pour House, Kings, Slim's and Lincoln Theatre are all within a few blocks.
alternatives.rain: Same walk, but the forecast has thunderstorms; carry a folding umbrella. Every listed stop is indoors, so a storm costs you nothing but the sidewalk.

alternatives.good_weather: City Plaza outdoor sets.
alternatives.rain: Move to the club shows — Lincoln Theatre and the Pour House both run full indoor Hopscotch nights.

practical_notes: Park once in a downtown deck (Moore Square or Charter Square) and walk; street parking is scarce on a festival Saturday.
The three day parties are genuinely free and do not require a festival wristband — that is the whole point of this plan.
Wristband City is at Church on Morgan, 136 E. Morgan St, if you decide to buy in for the evening.
Thunderstorms are forecast; the itinerary is deliberately indoor-heavy.

itineraries.title: Two Oktoberfests, One Durham Saturday
itineraries.theme: Farmers market, tobacco history, and Durham's two competing Oktoberfests
itineraries.cost_range: $20-$70 depending on beer and a Bulls ticket
itineraries.overview: Durham is running two Oktoberfests on the same Saturday — Motorco's sixteenth and the Glass Jug's twelfth — about six miles apart. You can do one properly, or do both if you pace yourself. Wrap it around the Saturday farmers market in the morning and a Bulls game at night.

morning.title: "Field & Factory: A Look at Tobacco's Laborers" at Duke Homestead
morning.notes: Free historic-site program on the people who actually worked the tobacco. Ten minutes north of downtown.

afternoon.title: 12th Annual Oktoberfest at The Glass Jug
afternoon.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab, RTP
afternoon.notes: German-style pours, food and games, running all day at the RTP beer lab.

afternoon.title: 16th Annual Durham Oktoberfest at Motorco
afternoon.notes: The downtown one, in the lot and the music hall. If you're only doing one, do this — it's walkable from the market and dinner.

afternoon.title: You Are Not Alone Youth Festival
afternoon.notes: Free youth mental-health festival across the street from the market pavilion — an easy, sober detour if you're with kids.

evening.title: Nana Grizol / Middnightt / Kym Register
evening.notes: Early show — Athens indie-folk with Durham's own Kym Register. Done in time for the ballgame.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs. Nashville Sounds
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St
evening.notes: Last home game of the homestand. Pick this or the Pinhook, not both.

evening.title: BODY ROLL DANCE PARTY
evening.notes: $5 at the door, runs late. The natural landing spot after either the game or the Oktoberfest.

food.notes: Producer-only market with hot-food vendors; ask at the stall rather than assuming. Free to walk in.

food.place: Oktoberfest food at Motorco or The Glass Jug
food.vegan_dish: unknown — check what the day's vendors are serving
food.vegetarian_dish: unknown — check what the day's vendors are serving
food.notes: Both festivals run their own food; neither published a menu in advance, so treat the vegan/veg option as unconfirmed until you're there.
Wood-fired pizza on West Main, walkable from the Pinhook and the ballpark. Menu changes seasonally — check the board for the night's vegetarian pie.

alternatives.good_weather: Motorco's lot party is mostly outdoors — take it.
alternatives.rain: Motorco moves inside the music hall, and the Glass Jug has an indoor taproom. Neither cancels for weather.

alternatives.good_weather: Sit down the third-base line for the sunset.
alternatives.rain: Thunderstorms are forecast and minor-league games do get delayed — have the Pinhook early show (5pm, $15) as your indoor fallback.

alternatives.good_weather: The tour uses the outdoor farm buildings.
alternatives.rain: Swap for the Carolina Theatre — Pepito and the Trash Cans at 11am if you have kids along.

practical_notes: Motorco and the Glass Jug's RTP lab are about 15 minutes apart by car; don't try to drive between them after drinking at both.
Downtown Durham parking: the Foster Street and Rigsbee decks put you within a block of the market, Motorco and Central Park.
The Bulls game is the last of the homestand — they're at Worcester after this.
Storms are forecast; the ballgame is the only leg genuinely exposed to a delay.

itineraries.title: Cary: Circus in the Park, Film in the Theater
itineraries.theme: A free outdoor circus festival bookended by a film festival and a vintage market
itineraries.cost_range: $0-$50 — most of the day is free
itineraries.overview: Downtown Cary has stacked a vintage market, a free circus arts festival and the third night of the BEYOND film festival into eight walkable blocks. Everything except the film tickets is free, and the whole thing sits within a few minutes' walk of the Cary Theater.

morning.title: Cary Farmers Market
morning.notes: Producer-only Saturday market on East Park Street. Breakfast and coffee here.

afternoon.title: The Cary Vintage Market
afternoon.notes: Clothing, records, furniture and oddities in the park.

afternoon.title: Healing Colors & Sounds Art Exhibition
afternoon.notes: A quiet indoor stop three minutes' walk from the park.

afternoon.title: Ripple Effects: Shorts (BEYOND festival)
afternoon.location: The Cary Theater, 122 E Chatham St
afternoon.notes: A shorts block if the afternoon heat gets to you — the theater is air conditioned.

afternoon.title: Carolina Circus Festival: The Greatest Show
afternoon.notes: Aerialists, jugglers and clowns, free and outdoors. The centerpiece of the day.

evening.title: BEYOND: The Cary Film Festival — night three
evening.notes: Feature programming at the Cary Theater.

evening.title: Trivia Night with Hammered Trivia
evening.notes: Free trivia in the same building if the film isn't your thing.

evening.title: Whiskey, Wine & Fire
evening.notes: The 21+ alternative to the whole downtown plan — live-fire cooking and tastings on the Koka Booth lawn, ten minutes away by car.

food.notes: Ask at the stall. The market is free to enter.

food.vegan_dish: unknown — festival vendors are not published in advance
food.vegetarian_dish: unknown — festival vendors are not published in advance
food.notes: The vintage market and circus festival both bring vendors into the park. Treat the vegan option as unconfirmed until you see the trucks.
A block from the Cary Theater. This is a neighborhood pointer, not a verified menu — check what's open before the 7pm screening.

alternatives.good_weather: Downtown Cary Park lawn — bring a blanket.
alternatives.rain: Thunderstorms are in the forecast. Fall back to the Cary Theater: the Ripple Effects shorts block at 2pm and Mishaps & Misadventures at 5:30pm both run indoors.

alternatives.good_weather: Browse the park stalls.
alternatives.rain: Page-Walker Arts & History Center's Healing Colors & Sounds exhibition is indoors and two minutes away.

alternatives.leg: Whiskey, Wine & Fire at Koka Booth
alternatives.good_weather: Lawn seating, outdoor cooking stations.
alternatives.rain: Koka Booth is an open-air amphitheater — check their event page before driving out if storms have set in.

practical_notes: Downtown Cary Park has a parking deck; the farmers market, vintage market, circus festival and Cary Theater are all within a five-minute walk of it.
BEYOND runs Thursday through Sunday — Saturday is the busiest programming day.
Whiskey, Wine & Fire is 21+; the downtown plan is not.
Storms are forecast for the afternoon — the Cary Theater is the indoor escape hatch and it's central.

itineraries.title: Chapel Hill Game Day into Greek Tragedy
itineraries.theme: Noon kickoff at Kenan, then Sophocles or a free symphony on the green
itineraries.cost_range: $20-$90 depending on football and theatre tickets
itineraries.overview: A noon UNC kickoff frees the whole evening, and Chapel Hill has two very different things to do with it: PlayMakers' opening night of Oedipus, or the North Carolina Symphony playing free on the Southern Village green. Carrboro's clubs are the late option.

morning.title: Kids' Dog Show
morning.location: Henry Anderson III Community Park, Carrboro
morning.notes: Only if you have kids and aren't going to the game — costumes, tricks and ribbons at the small dog park.

afternoon.title: North Carolina Football vs East Tennessee State
afternoon.notes: Noon kickoff. Non-conference game, so tickets should be findable.

afternoon.title: Carrboro Farmers Market
afternoon.notes: The pre-game move if you're up early — one of the oldest producer-only markets in the state, 8am to noon.

evening.title: Oedipus: King/Colonus — opening night
evening.location: Joan H. Gillings Center for Dramatic Art, 120 Country Club Rd
evening.notes: PlayMakers' opening night of the Sophocles cycle. On campus, so you can leave the car where you parked for the game.

evening.title: Patriotic Pops Celebrating America 250 with the North Carolina Symphony
evening.notes: The free alternative — full symphony on the green in Southern Village, about ten minutes south. Bring chairs.

evening.title: Bring Out Yer Dead
evening.location: Cat's Cradle, 300 E Main St, Carrboro
evening.notes: Grateful Dead tribute on the Cradle main stage if you want a late night in Carrboro instead.

food.notes: Producer-only market, 8am-noon on the Town Commons. Ask at the stall.
Walkable from Kenan Stadium. A neighborhood pointer, not a verified menu — note that Mediterranean Deli's Chapel Hill location lists itself as closed pending a re-opening, so don't plan on it.
Next to Cat's Cradle and the ArtsCenter. Check current menus — this is a location recommendation, not a verified dish.

alternatives.good_weather: Ninety-degree noon kickoff — the west stands get shade first. Bring water.
alternatives.rain: Thunderstorms are forecast; college football plays through rain but lightning stops play. Have the Ackland's Artist Conversation (Sunday 2pm) or an indoor Franklin Street afternoon as the backup.

alternatives.leg: Patriotic Pops on Southern Village Green (outdoors, free)
alternatives.good_weather: Chairs and a blanket on the green.
alternatives.rain: Switch to PlayMakers' Oedipus opening night indoors at the Gillings Center — same 7:30 curtain, tickets from $20.

practical_notes: A noon kickoff means campus parking fills early; the Rams Head and Craige decks are the usual options.
The Gillings Center is a walk from the stadium — one parking spot covers both if you're doing football then theatre.
Southern Village is about ten minutes south on 15-501 and has its own free lot.
Ninety degrees with afternoon storms: shade, water and a rain layer for the stadium.

itineraries.title: Chatham County Pepper Sunday
itineraries.theme: PepperFest, a pottery kiln yard, and tigers at dusk

weather.summary: Slight Chance Rain Showers then Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.overview: Chatham County's nineteenth PepperFest is the anchor — local chefs cooking with local peppers at The Plant — and it happens to fall on a day when Mark Hewitt opens his kiln yard and Carolina Tiger Rescue runs its twilight tour. Three things you can't do any other week, inside twelve miles of each other.

morning.title: Mark Hewitt Pottery LocoPops & Pottery Pop-Up
morning.location: Mark Hewitt Pottery, 424 Johnny Burke Rd
morning.notes: One of the country's best-known wood-fire potters opens the kiln yard, with LocoPops on hand. No listed start time — check before you go.

afternoon.title: 19th Annual PepperFest
afternoon.notes: Local chefs cook with peppers from local farms, with music and beer. Buy tickets ahead — this one sells out.

evening.title: Twilight Tours at Carolina Tiger Rescue
evening.location: Carolina Tiger Rescue, 1940 Hanks Chapel Rd
evening.notes: Guided sanctuary tour at the hour the big cats actually get moving. Reservation required — book before you leave the house.

food.place: Downtown Pittsboro cafés, around the courthouse circle
food.notes: A neighborhood pointer, not a verified menu. Sunday hours vary in Pittsboro — check before you count on it.

food.vegan_dish: unknown — the chef lineup is published on the day
food.vegetarian_dish: unknown — but a pepper festival built on local farms reliably has produce-forward plates
food.notes: This is lunch. Go hungry; it's a tasting-plate format across many chefs.
120 Lowes Dr, on the way back toward 64. Check the current menu — the dish list isn't published online.

alternatives.good_weather: Full run of the outdoor tasting stations and music.
alternatives.rain: Scattered storms are forecast. The Plant has covered areas but this is fundamentally an outdoor festival — check their page the morning of.

alternatives.good_weather: The whole tour is on outdoor paths; dusk is when the cats are active.
alternatives.rain: Tours run rain or shine but the sanctuary can cancel for lightning — call ahead, and have Carolina Brewery's taproom as the fallback.

alternatives.good_weather: Wander the yard and the seconds tables.
alternatives.rain: The pop-up runs Saturday and Sunday, so shift to Saturday if Sunday looks bad.

practical_notes: Book the Carolina Tiger Rescue tour in advance — it's reservation-only and small.
PepperFest tickets are worth buying ahead; it's the biggest food event in the county.
Pittsboro is about 45 minutes from Raleigh on 64 West; the three stops are within about twelve miles of each other.
Cell service is patchy on the back roads out to Hanks Chapel and Johnny Burke — screenshot your directions.

itineraries.title: Museum Park Family Friday
itineraries.theme: A free, low-cost kid day across Raleigh's museum campuses

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.overview: Almost everything here is free, and it's built for a 94-degree day: outdoor programs land in the cool morning, then you're inside museums for the hot part of the afternoon. Prairie Ridge, the arboretum, the Museum of Natural Sciences and the NCMA are all within fifteen minutes of each other.

morning.title: Birdwatching for Beginners
morning.location: Prairie Ridge Ecostation, 1671 Gold Star Dr
morning.notes: Loaner binoculars available. Go early — it's the coolest part of a 94-degree day.

morning.title: Garden Storytime
morning.notes: The younger-kid alternative to birding, four minutes away.

morning.title: Activate Good's 9/11 Day of Service & Remembrance
morning.notes: If your kids are old enough to volunteer, this is the day's most substantial thing to do.

afternoon.title: In the Moment: Cultural Activities for the Memory Community
afternoon.notes: Free, air-conditioned, and specifically designed for visitors living with memory loss and their care partners — worth knowing about if that's your family.

afternoon.title: Incredible Science
afternoon.location: NC Museum of Natural Sciences, 11 W Jones St
afternoon.notes: A short live demo in the Daily Planet. The museum itself is free and indoors — the obvious heat shelter.

afternoon.title: Dungeons and Dragons
afternoon.notes: Free open D&D for older kids and teens.

evening.title: Live Music Fridays
evening.notes: Free live music, family-tolerant early in the evening.

evening.title: Hairspray
evening.location: Cantey V. Sutton Theatre, 301 Pogue St
evening.notes: Raleigh Little Theatre's musical — the one paid thing on this list. Adult $33-36; senior, student and military $30-33.

food.place: Home, or a Hillsborough Street café
food.notes: Eat before the 10am programs — Prairie Ridge has no food service.

food.place: Iris at the NC Museum of Art / the museum café
food.notes: On site at the NCMA so you don't lose the afternoon to a drive. Menu not published in a form we could verify — check on arrival.

food.vegan_dish: Chicken and Waffles ($16.50) — vegan; or Homestyle Meatloaf ($22)
food.vegetarian_dish: Fried Pimento Cheese ($11) to start, Risotto ($21.50) to follow
food.notes: 2431-103 Crabtree Blvd. Entirely vegetarian and vegan, which makes a mixed-diet family dinner simple.

alternatives.good_weather: Mostly sunny and 94 — go at 10am and be done before the heat.
alternatives.rain: Slight chance of afternoon storms only; morning should hold. If it doesn't, the Museum of Natural Sciences downtown is free and indoors.

alternatives.good_weather: Shaded beds and borders keep it bearable.
alternatives.rain: Swap for the NCMA's indoor galleries — free admission to the permanent collection.

alternatives.good_weather: Volunteer projects run on the park lawns.
alternatives.rain: Check Activate Good's page; service days often relocate rather than cancel.

practical_notes: It's 94 degrees — front-load the outdoor stops and treat the museums as afternoon air conditioning.
Both the NCMA and the Museum of Natural Sciences are free for general admission.
Prairie Ridge is the museum's satellite site off Blue Ridge Road, not the downtown building — don't mix them up.
Raleigh Little Theatre is the only ticketed item here; buy ahead.

itineraries.title: Durham Sunday, Slow
itineraries.theme: Open studio, a matinee ballgame, and a Simpsons writer cooking dinner

weather.summary: Slight Chance Rain Showers then Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.overview: An unhurried Durham Sunday: free drop-in art at the Nasher, a 1:05 matinee at the DBAP, and — genuinely — Simpsons writer Bill Oakley hosting a Steamed Hams dinner at Fullsteam. Short distances, no rushing.

morning.title: Duke University Women's Soccer vs Stanford — Youth Day
morning.notes: Noon kickoff against Stanford, with youth-day programming. The alternative to the Bulls if you'd rather watch soccer.

afternoon.title: Second Sundays: Open Studio
afternoon.location: Nasher Museum of Art, 2001 Campus Dr
afternoon.notes: Free drop-in art making for all ages in the Nasher studio. Two hours, no registration.

afternoon.title: Durham Bulls vs. Nashville Sounds
afternoon.notes: Sunday matinee — the last game of the homestand. Pick this or the Nasher.

afternoon.title: Duke University Field Hockey vs VCU
afternoon.location: Williams Field at Jack Katz Stadium
afternoon.notes: Jr. Iron Dukes day with postgame autographs — a good third option if you have kids.

evening.title: Bill Oakley Presents: Steamed Hams — The Fabulous Dinner Event
evening.notes: The Simpsons writer and fast-food critic hosts a Steamed Hams themed dinner. Ticketed; book ahead.

evening.title: Wind Walkers
evening.notes: Metalcore next door to Fullsteam, if dinner isn't the plan.

evening.title: Alex Cameron / Josh De Costa
evening.notes: Australian art-pop downtown — the quieter late option.

food.vegan_dish: unknown — the current menu is only published through their ordering system
food.notes: Durham's default Sunday breakfast. We could not verify specific dishes; check the live menu.

food.place: Durham Bulls Athletic Park concessions, or the Nasher café
food.notes: Depends which afternoon you pick. Neither publishes a menu we could verify.

food.place: Fullsteam Brewery — Bill Oakley's Steamed Hams dinner
food.vegan_dish: unknown — it is a themed set dinner; ask when booking
food.notes: This is dinner and the evening's entertainment in one. If the set menu doesn't work for your diet, Fullsteam's regular taproom and the Rigsbee Avenue food trucks are right there.

alternatives.good_weather: Sunday afternoon at the DBAP, 89 degrees — sit on the shaded side.
alternatives.rain: Scattered storms are forecast and matinees do get delayed. The Nasher open studio at 1pm is free, indoors and two miles away.

alternatives.good_weather: Both are free-standing outdoor stadiums; noon and 1pm starts.
alternatives.rain: Duke's swimming and diving Blue/White Week is indoors at Taishoff the same day.

alternatives.good_weather: Rigsbee Avenue is walkable between Fullsteam and Motorco.
alternatives.rain: Both are indoors — no change needed.

practical_notes: Fullsteam and Motorco are next door to each other on Rigsbee Avenue; one parking spot covers both.
The Nasher is on Duke's campus, about ten minutes from downtown, with its own free lot on Sundays.
Bill Oakley's dinner is ticketed and small — book before Sunday.
This is the Bulls' last home game before a road trip to Worcester.

itineraries.title: Wake Forest & North Raleigh, Free All Day
itineraries.theme: Two farmers markets, a free arts celebration, and a street party the night before
itineraries.overview: The quiet-side alternative to Hopscotch weekend. Wake Forest's Community Celebration of the Arts is free, so is the farmers market, and Sunday's Concert in the Park at Joyner is free too. If you can move it a night earlier, Friday Night on White is the town's best street party.

morning.title: Wake Forest Farmers' Market
morning.notes: 8am to noon on South White Street. Breakfast and produce.

morning.title: Community Celebration of the Arts
morning.location: Wake Forest Renaissance Centre, 405 S Brooks St
morning.notes: Free performances, demonstrations and hands-on activities. Runs to 2pm, indoors and out.

afternoon.title: Healing Colors & Sounds / gallery time
afternoon.location: Gregg Museum of Art & Design, 1903 Hillsborough St, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina's Black Heritage — free, indoors and on the way back into Raleigh.

afternoon.title: Downtown Raleigh Black History Tour
afternoon.notes: A walking tour from the Pope House if you'd rather spend the afternoon downtown.

evening.title: Cultus Black / Outliar / HammerFall at Chapel of Bones
evening.location: Chapel of Bones, 658 Maywood Ave, Raleigh
evening.notes: HammerFall headline at 6:30. Raleigh's south-side metal room, well clear of the Hopscotch crowds.

evening.title: Air Supply – A Matter of Time Tour
evening.notes: The opposite end of the spectrum, downtown.

evening.title: Friday Night on White (the night before)
evening.notes: If you can shift a day: free street party on South White Street, live band, food trucks, beer garden, Friday 6-9pm.

food.place: Wake Forest Farmers' Market prepared-food vendors
food.notes: Free to walk in; ask at the stall.

food.vegan_dish: unknown — ask which market sides are dairy-free
food.vegetarian_dish: Spanakopita with two sides ($12.99), or the Stuffed Eggplant (veggie) with two sides ($12.99) on Sundays
food.notes: 9650 Strickland Rd, Suite 149 — on the way back from Wake Forest. Lebanese; the market sides counter is where the vegetarian options live.

food.place: Downtown Wake Forest, South White Street
food.notes: A location pointer, not a verified menu. If you're heading back into Raleigh for a show, eat before you drive.

alternatives.good_weather: South White Street, 8am to noon.
alternatives.rain: Storms are forecast for the afternoon; the morning market should be fine. The Renaissance Centre's arts celebration is partly indoors either way.

alternatives.good_weather: Indoor and outdoor activities across the Renaissance Centre.
alternatives.rain: The Centre itself is indoors — the celebration continues.

alternatives.leg: Friday Night on White (outdoors, the night before)
alternatives.good_weather: Street closed, band on, beer garden open.
alternatives.rain: Friday's forecast is mostly sunny with only a slight chance of storms — the better weather bet of the two evenings.

practical_notes: Wake Forest is about 25 minutes up Capital Boulevard from downtown Raleigh; the market, Renaissance Centre and White Street are all walkable from each other.
The whole daytime plan is free — this is the cheapest itinerary of the week.
Concert in the Park at E. Carroll Joyner Park is Sunday 5:30pm and also free, if you'd rather make it a weekend.
Hopscotch is happening downtown the same night; expect Raleigh traffic and parking to be worse than usual after 6pm.
